Let $k$ be a field. A **Lie algebra over $k$** is a $k$-vector space
$\mathfrak g$ ([[def-vector-space]]) together with a map

$$[-,-]:\mathfrak g\times\mathfrak g\longrightarrow\mathfrak g$$

that is linear in each variable ([[def-linear-map]]) and satisfies, for all
$x,y,z\in\mathfrak g$,

$$[x,x]=0$$

and

$$[x,[y,z]]+[y,[z,x]]+[z,[x,y]]=0.$$

The first identity is **alternation** and the second is the **Jacobi identity**.
No finite-dimensional hypothesis is imposed. Alternation implies
$[x,y]=-[y,x]$ in every characteristic: expand
$0=[x+y,x+y]=[x,y]+[y,x]$. Thus skew-symmetry is a consequence here, not a
replacement for alternation in characteristic $2$.

The zero vector space, with its unique bracket, is a Lie algebra. A Lie algebra
is **abelian** when $[x,y]=0$ for every $x,y$.

For a vector space $V$ over $k$, write

$$\mathfrak{gl}(V)=\operatorname{End}_k(V)$$

with commutator bracket $[A,B]=AB-BA$. Expansion of triple composites shows
that this is a Lie algebra in every characteristic.

A **representation** of a Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ on $V$ is a Lie-algebra
homomorphism

$$\rho:\mathfrak g\longrightarrow\mathfrak{gl}(V).$$

Writing $xv$ for $\rho(x)(v)$, this is equivalently a $k$-bilinear action
$\mathfrak g\times V\to V$ satisfying

$$[x,y]v=x(yv)-y(xv)$$

for all $x,y\in\mathfrak g$ and $v\in V$. No finite-dimensional hypothesis is
imposed on either $\mathfrak g$ or $V$. The zero vector space and the zero
action are allowed.

Restriction along $\iota_{\mathfrak g}:\mathfrak g\to U(\mathfrak g)$ and extension by the
universal property give mutually inverse correspondences between
representations of $\mathfrak g$ and unital left $U(\mathfrak g)$-module
structures whose restriction along $k\to U(\mathfrak g)$ is the given scalar
action on $V$. A linear map is an intertwiner on one side exactly when it is a
module homomorphism on the other.

Let $k$ be a field, let $A$ be a unital associative $k$-algebra
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]), and let $V$ be a $k$-vector space.
Write $\operatorname{End}_k(V)=\mathcal L_k(V,V)$ for the $k$-linear endomorphisms
of $V$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); its multiplication is composition
and its identity is $\operatorname{id}_V$
([[def-endomorphism-ring-of-a-module]], [[prop-endomorphisms-form-a-ring]]).
An **(unital) representation of $A$ on $V$** is a $k$-linear map
$$\rho:A\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_k(V)$$
such that $\rho(1_A)=\operatorname{id}_V$ and
$$\rho(ab)=\rho(a)\circ\rho(b)\qquad(a,b\in A).$$
The associated action is $a\cdot v:=\rho(a)(v)$. The zero vector space is
allowed; in that case $\operatorname{id}_V=0$.

Let $R$ be a ring. A **left $R$-module** is an abelian group $(M,+,0_M)$ with a
scalar action $R\times M\to M$, $(r,m)\mapsto rm$, satisfying

$$r(m+n)=rm+rn,\quad (r+s)m=rm+sm,\quad (rs)m=r(sm),\quad 1_Rm=m.$$

A **right $R$-module** has an action $M\times R\to M$, $(m,r)\mapsto mr$, with
the analogous right-handed axioms. Unless “right” is stated, **module** means a
unital left module.

Let $F$ be a field ([[def-field]]), with additive identity $0_F$, multiplicative
identity $1_F$, and the field axioms as stated there. A **vector space over $F$**,
also called an **$F$-vector space**, consists of

- a set $V$, whose elements are called **vectors**;
- a binary operation $+ : V \times V \to V$ on $V$ ([[def-binary-operation]]),
  the **vector addition**;
- an element $0_V \in V$, the **zero vector**;
- a map $\cdot \,:\, F \times V \to V$, the **scalar multiplication**, written
  $\lambda v := \cdot(\lambda, v)$;

subject to the following axioms, in which $u, v \in V$ and $\lambda, \mu \in F$
are arbitrary.

- **(V1)** $(V, +, 0_V)$ is an abelian group ([[def-group]]): $+$ is associative
  and commutative, $0_V$ is a two-sided identity for $+$
  ([[def-identity-element]]), and every $v \in V$ has an additive inverse
  ([[def-invertible-element]]).
- **(V2)** $\lambda(u + v) = \lambda u + \lambda v$.
- **(V3)** $(\lambda + \mu)v = \lambda v + \mu v$.
- **(V4)** $(\lambda\mu)v = \lambda(\mu v)$.
- **(V5)** $1_F v = v$.

The elements of $F$ are called **scalars**. When several vector spaces are in
play we write $0_V$ for the zero of $V$, and we write $-v$ for the additive
inverse of $v$ and $u - v := u + (-v)$.

**The notation $0_V$ and $-v$ is legitimate.** Axiom (V1) asserts only that some
two-sided identity and some additive inverses exist. That there is at most one
two-sided identity for $+$ is [[lem-identity-unique]], and that an invertible
element of a monoid has exactly one inverse is [[lem-inverse-unique]]; both are
proved before [[def-group]] and are inherited here with the group structure. So
$0_V$ and $-v$ denote well-defined elements, and nothing below re-derives them.

**What (V1) buys, and why it is not restated.** Associativity, commutativity, the
identity law $v + 0_V = v = 0_V + v$, the inverse law $v + (-v) = 0_V$,
cancellation ([[lem-group-cancellation]]) and the inverse identities
([[lem-group-inverse-laws]]) are facts about abelian groups. They are quoted from
the group page wherever they are used and are never proved again for vectors.

Let $V$ and $W$ be vector spaces over the same field $F$. Write

$$\mathcal L(V,W):=\{T:V\to W:T\text{ is linear}\}.$$

For $S,T\in\mathcal L(V,W)$ and $\lambda\in F$, define pointwise operations by

$$(S+T)(v):=S(v)+T(v),\qquad (\lambda T)(v):=\lambda T(v).$$

The zero function $v\mapsto0_W$ is denoted by $0$. Closure and the vector-space
axioms for these operations are proved in [[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]].

Let $R$ be a commutative ring ([[def-commutative-ring]]). An **$R$-algebra** is a unital ring $A$ together with a unital ring homomorphism

$$\eta_A:R\longrightarrow A$$

([[def-ring-homomorphism]]) whose image is central: $\eta_A(r)a=a\eta_A(r)$ for every $r\in R$ and $a\in A$. The induced scalar action is $ra:=\eta_A(r)a$, making $A$ an $R$-module and multiplication $A\times A\to A$ bilinear.

An **$R$-algebra homomorphism** $f:A\to B$ is a unital ring homomorphism satisfying $f\circ\eta_A=\eta_B$. Such a map is automatically $R$-linear. An $R$-algebra is **commutative** when its underlying ring is commutative.

Let $k$ be any field.

1. For any group $G$, the vector space $kG$ of finite sums $\sum_{g\in G}a_g g$ is a Hopf algebra. Its multiplication is the bilinear extension of the group law, its unit is the group identity $e$, and
   $$\Delta(g)=g\otimes g,\qquad \varepsilon(g)=1,\qquad S(g)=g^{-1}\quad(g\in G).$$
2. For any finite group $G$, the pointwise algebra $k^G$ of all functions $f:G\to k$ is a Hopf algebra with
   $$\Delta(f)(x,y)=f(xy),\qquad \varepsilon(f)=f(e),\qquad S(f)(x)=f(x^{-1}).$$
   The finite-set tensor identification $k^G\otimes k^G\cong k^{G\times G}$ is used to define $\Delta$. No Hopf structure on the full function space $k^G$ for infinite $G$ is claimed.
3. The polynomial algebra $k[x]$ is a Hopf algebra with
   $$\Delta(x)=x\otimes1+1\otimes x,\qquad \varepsilon(x)=0,\qquad S(x)=-x.$$
   These formulas work in every characteristic. The element $x$ is primitive in every characteristic, and in characteristic $p>0$ so is $x^p$.

A **Hopf algebra over $k$** is a bialgebra $H$ together with a $k$-linear map $S:H\to H$, called its **antipode**, such that

$$S*\mathrm{id}_H=u\varepsilon=\mathrm{id}_H*S,$$

where $*$ is the convolution product on $\operatorname{Hom}_k(H,H)$, $u:k\to H$ is the unit, and $\varepsilon:H\to k$ is the counit. Equivalently, $m(S\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta=u\varepsilon=m(\mathrm{id}\otimes S)\Delta$. Thus $S$ is the two-sided inverse of $\mathrm{id}_H$ in the convolution algebra. This definition imposes no compositional bijectivity condition on $S$.

Let $k$ be a field, let $A$ be a unital associative $k$-algebra
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]), and let $V$ be a $k$-vector space.
Write $\operatorname{End}_k(V)=\mathcal L_k(V,V)$ for the $k$-linear endomorphisms
of $V$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); its multiplication is composition
and its identity is $\operatorname{id}_V$
([[def-endomorphism-ring-of-a-module]], [[prop-endomorphisms-form-a-ring]]).
An **(unital) representation of $A$ on $V$** is a $k$-linear map
$$\rho:A\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_k(V)$$
such that $\rho(1_A)=\operatorname{id}_V$ and
$$\rho(ab)=\rho(a)\circ\rho(b)\qquad(a,b\in A).$$
The associated action is $a\cdot v:=\rho(a)(v)$. The zero vector space is
allowed; in that case $\operatorname{id}_V=0$.

Let $k$ be a field, $A$ a unital associative $k$-algebra, and $V$ a
$k$-vector space. There is a bijection between unital representations
$\rho:A\to\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ of [[def-unital-associative-algebra-representation]]
and $k$-bilinear left $A$-module actions $A\times V\to V$, $(a,v)\mapsto a\cdot v$,
for which $(ab)\cdot v=a\cdot(b\cdot v)$ and $1_A\cdot v=v$. The maps are
$a\cdot v=\rho(a)(v)$ and $\rho(a)(v)=a\cdot v$. Here $k$-bilinear means
linear in each variable with respect to the given $k$-vector structures; the
module axioms are those of [[def-left-and-right-modules]].

Let $k$ be a field and let $H$ be a $k$-vector space with associative unital multiplication $m$, unit $1_H$, coassociative comultiplication $\Delta:H\to H\otimes_k H$, and counit $\varepsilon:H\to k$. Assume $\Delta$ and $\varepsilon$ are unital algebra maps; this is the bialgebra interface used on this page. A left $H$-module is a unital left module in the sense of [[def-left-and-right-modules]]: its action satisfies $1_Hv=v$ and $(hh')v=h(h'v)$. Let $H\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ be the category whose objects are all left $H$-modules and whose morphisms $f:V\to W$ are $k$-linear maps satisfying $f(hv)=h f(v)$ for every $h\in H$ and $v\in V$.

For left $H$-modules $V,W$, give the algebraic tensor product $V\otimes_k W$ the candidate action

$$h\cdot(v\otimes w)=\sum h_{(1)}v\otimes h_{(2)}w,\qquad \Delta(h)=\sum h_{(1)}\otimes h_{(2)}.$$

The sums are finite algebraic tensor sums; the tensor product and scalar conventions are those of [[def-hh-scalar-and-tensor-conventions]]. The candidate unit object is $k_\varepsilon=k$ with $h\cdot c=\varepsilon(h)c$. For morphisms $f:V\to V'$ and $g:W\to W'$, the candidate tensor morphism is the usual linear map $f\otimes g$ determined by $(f\otimes g)(v\otimes w)=f(v)\otimes g(w)$ through [[thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products]].

These formulas specify the proposed tensor operations; [[thm-hh-bialgebra-module-tensor-coherence]] proves that they are module actions and that the canonical associator and unit maps are morphisms in $H\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $L,M,N$ be $R$-modules. There are natural $R$-module isomorphisms

$$\sigma_{M,N}:M\otimes_RN\longrightarrow N\otimes_RM,\qquad \sigma_{M,N}(m\otimes n)=n\otimes m,$$

and

$$\alpha_{L,M,N}:(L\otimes_RM)\otimes_RN\longrightarrow L\otimes_R(M\otimes_RN),\qquad \alpha((l\otimes m)\otimes n)=l\otimes(m\otimes n).$$

Moreover $\sigma_{N,M}\sigma_{M,N}$ is the identity.
